national.title: Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut
national.summary: The company behind the Claude chatbot will become one of the most valuable firms in the world.
national.body:
Anthropic, the company behind AI chatbot Claude, has raised a record $81bn (£62.bn) in a stock market debut that will make it one of the most valuable companies in the world.

A surge of investor appetite to buy shares in the loss-making business meant more stock was sold than originally planned. Anthropic's shares have been priced at $83, up from the proposed $70-$78 range.

Shares will begin trading later on Thursday in New York, valuing the five year-old firm at around $1.5 trillion.

The flotation is being seen as a crucial test for fast-growing AI sector. Anthropic is the first purely AI-focused firm to publicly sell its shares.

Vast amounts of money have been poured into AI infrastructure and the development of AI based tools. But questions are being raised over whether and when those investments will pay off.

The seven founders, who set up Anthropic up in 2021, will become multi-billionaires immediately.

The firm said earlier this month it would offer its shares for between $70 and $78 each, which would have valued the company at up to $1.3tn.

But demand for Anthropic's stock debut - commonly referred to as its initial public offering, or IPO - is very high, according to one early investor in the company who spoke to the BBC on condition of anonymity.

national.title: Trump, Xi and Putin sit down for rare three-way meeting in China
national.summary: President Trump, China's President Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin sat down for a rare meeting in China, with nuclear weapons and the Ukraine and Iran wars on the agenda.
national.body: President Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin sat down for a meeting in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday — a rare face-to-face encounter for the leaders of three of the world's most powerful countries.All three made brief opening statements before meeting behind closed doors for about an hour and a half. The leaders did not offer joint or separate statements to reporters after the sit-down, and Mr. Trump immediately left for the airport to return home.Before the gathering, Mr. Trump met separately with Putin on the sidelines of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, and then with Xi."We've had a great relationship for many years," Mr. Trump said, standing alongside his Russian counterpart. "I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this, or at least start."Cameras captured Mr. Trump, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent entering a small conference room in Shenzhen to meet with Putin, Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and other Russian officials. As Mr. Trump approached Putin for a handshake, he said, "Who is that?" before laughing and saying, "He's my friend."Russia's TASS news agency said the war in Ukraine was the main topic discussed by the two leaders, and that Putin left the meeting in "an excellent mood."Mr. Trump then met for about an hour with Xi ahead of the three-way meeting. As the Trump-Xi session began, Xi told Mr. Trump relations between China and the United States were "stable and improved."Mr. Trump told reporters he had spoken with Xi for two hours on Wednesday, with trade and tariffs being ethe main topics. He also said he would be asking China to "do some more" for American farmers, because China has an "insatiable appetite." He said he intended to discuss ending the Ukraine war with Xi and Putin.Mr. Trump said previously that he planned to talk about denuclearization with his fellow leaders. Russia and the United States are by far the world's three largest holders of nuclear weapons, with stockpiles estimated at well over 5,000 warheads, while China is beleived to be a distant third, with about 600 weapons. national.title: Obama gives pep talk to freshman House Democrats in surprise visit
national.summary: The former president was the surprise guest at a hastily called meeting of Democrats who just won House seats.
national.body: Washington — Groups of newly elected Democratic members of the House of Representatives rushed to board buses outside the Capitol on Wednesday bound for a meeting with a "special guest." When they arrived at their destination, they learned the guest was none other than former President Barack Obama."I did not know who the special guest was, but I knew it was going to be someone special," Representative-Elect Johnny Garcia, of Texas, told CBS News. "And then obviously we get here, and we get to see it's President Obama!"The meeting was arranged by House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, fresh off his nomination to become the next House speaker. If elected in January, he would make history as the first African American to serve in the role."We're excited about the opportunities that are in front of us to deliver big, meaningful bold progress to the American people," Jeffries said as he introduced Obama to cheers and chants of "four more years." "I believe in the Constitution, people," Obama quipped.The former President engaged in a broad discussion, moderated by Jeffries, about the challenges and opportunities of the next Congress. Obama addressed practical matters, like having robust constituent services, and bigger picture policy goals such as lowering costs, making health care more affordable, and creating accessible housing, his office said. He also told the freshman class he was deeply proud of them, and encouraged them to stay connected to their communities.Representative-Elect Dr. Patty Garcia said the former president answered a "mix of questions" from new members including his advice to them, his message after this month's election victories, what the party can build on and immigration.Garcia first met Obama when he was a senator and she was a student at the University of Illinois. The incoming congresswoman said the event with the former president was a "full circle" moment as she prepares to represent a Chicago-area district."I think being able to see him in different roles, and you know, very encouraging message, of you know, 'You all represent different constituencies, very diverse, and at the end of the day, you need to kind of find a common ground that can help deliver for everyone as much as possible and make an impact,'" Garcia said. national.title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN
national.summary: Survivors reject relocation plans they say ignore their safety, land rights and livelihoods
national.body:
Survivors of a 2019 landslide in eastern Uganda that killed more than 50 people have taken their fight for relocation and compensation to the United Nations.

The 48 complainants accuse the government of violating Uganda's constitution by failing to put effective disaster management measures in Bududa, a mountainous district prone to landslides.

Their case comes as heavy rains raise the risk of further landslides. They say the government relocation programme ignores their safety, land rights and livelihoods.

The UN Human Rights Committee is considering what is believed to be the first case seeking climate adaptation measures, one that could set a global precedent.

The landslide struck Bududa in 2019, killing more than 53 people, including 33 children. Years later, survivors say every spell of heavy rain brings back fears of another tragedy.

William Tsama, one of the claimants, lost four members of his family members.

"Victims in such situations, ignored by governments, can take them to court to compel them to help their citizens."

Uganda introduced a resettlement plan for landslide-prone areas in 2011, but progress has been limited, with relatively few people relocated.

national.title: Dozens missing after boat carrying 100 migrants sinks off Senegal's coast
national.summary: Some local media report that at least four bodies have been recovered.
national.body:
Senegalese authorities are continuing search operations after a boat reportedly carrying about 100 migrants capsized off the coast.

Initial reports said that one person had died, but some local media have reported that at least four bodies have been recovered. Dozens of people are still missing.

Personal belongings were found on the badly damaged boat, which washed ashore near the village of Yenne, south of Dakar. Search operations continued throughout Wednesday and were due to resume on Thursday.

This comes less than two weeks after a shipwreck off the coast of the north-western town of Thieppe killed at least 39 people, in one of Senegal's deadliest migration disasters.

Oumar Sow, a representative of the village chief, said the latest tragedy happened around 02:00 local time (02:00 GMT).

"Cries could be heard coming from the pirogue that were audible even from the beach," the AFP news agency quoted him as saying.

A survivor questioned by the police said there were about 100 people on the boat, including five women, AFP reported.

Police recovered identity documents, several mobile phones and personal belongings from the wreckage, including a school enrolment document.

national.title: Crimean Bridge attacked again, Russia says
national.summary: The head of Crimea said traffic was suspended after another attack on the link between Russia and the occupied territory.
national.body:
The Crimean Bridge has been attacked by Ukraine for the third time this week, Russia has said.

The Moscow-installed head of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, said that rail traffic was temporarily suspended following another strike on the bridge connecting Russia to occupied Crimea.

On Tuesday, Ukrainian missiles and drones destroyed the central road section of the critical bridge, collapsing part of it into the water.

The important infrastructure has long been targeted by Ukraine because of its significance as a logistical and symbolic asset to Moscow's war effort.

It comes as Russian President Vladimir Putin meets US President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping on Thursday for landmark talks in China .

Aksyonov confirmed the strike on the bridge in the early hours of Thursday via Telegram.

Russia's transport ministry said nobody had been hurt in the attack, and that specialists were assessing damage to the bridge.

"As a result of a nighttime drone attack, train services on the railway section of the Crimean Bridge have been temporarily suspended," the ministry said in a statement on Telegram.

national.title: Iran ramps up attacks on Gulf countries after U.S. strikes
national.summary: America's Persian Gulf allies and oil tankers are under fire as Iran appears to lash out following U.S. strikes on a key island in the Strait of Hormuz.
national.body: The crisis in the Middle East sparked in February by the U.S and Israel bombing Iran has created the "largest threat" to energy security in history, the International Energy Agency (IEA) warned Thursday. The agency said in its flagship annual World Energy Outlook that consumers were increasingly footing the bill as the world runs out of ways to absorb the impact of the conflict on energy supplies. The crisis, just like previous energy shocks, would certainly leave "lasting marks", the agency warned. Gulf countries have been struggling to export oil since Iran began blockading the Strait of Hormuz and targeting tankers in the area. Despite attempts by the United States to escort vessels through vital channel — which before the war carried about one-fifth of global oil shipments — supply lines remain severely disrupted. "The Strait of Hormuz crisis has created the largest threat to energy security in history, one that dwarfs the scale of the oil shocks of the 1970s," IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol wrote in his foreword to the report. He highlighted the efforts countries had taken to protect households, with producing nations bringing more supplies into the market and using alternative routes, and China buying less from international markets. "Governments have intervened to try and provide some shelter for consumers, but they have nonetheless faced higher prices and, in some cases, shortfalls of supply," Birol wrote. The report said that "increasingly it is falling to consumers -- and high prices -- to absorb the impact as other buffers are run down". Birol had struck a more positive tone in July, when he wrote that the oil market was still benefiting from "several cushioning factors."

national.body:
Xi Jinping will believe he has achieved something no other world leader could in securing a historic summit with Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump in Shenzhen.

For decades, Washington and its western allies shaped the world order.

Yet it is China that has orchestrated the remarkable diplomatic spectacle of three of the world's most powerful protagonists sitting around the table.

And surrounding it all is the futuristic display that is Shenzhen, with driverless cars cruising past as drones fly overhead and robots - literally - dance in the streets.

Ostensibly, this is an economic summit for Asia Pacific leaders. But for Xi, it is also a demonstration of China's grip on the global economy and world politics.

His country is no longer just reacting to decisions made in Washington, London or Brussels - instead Beijing is at the heart of conversations which are reshaping the international order.

national.summary: Costco shoppers are stocking up on emergency items following a string of tech snafus, according to a Wall Street analyst.
national.body: Consumers are panic-buying at Costco, snapping up generators and other emergency-preparedness items in response to a recent string of technology outages, according to investment firm Mizuho Securities. "Consumer anxiety following the Microsoft Outlook outage, the ground stoppage for all U.S. airline flights, and apocalyptic concerns flaring up across social media have all contributed to increased emergency prep sales at Costco," Mizuho analyst David Bellinger wrote in a report. Shoppers are "pantry-loading," while 21 of the retailer's 26 "high-ticket generators" were sold out online as of Sunday night, he added. The recent outages, which blocked access to Microsoft apps, snarled flights nationwide and hindered banking activities at various times during the past week, are raising questions among Americans about a larger cybersecurity threat, CBS News chief correspondent Matt Gutman said on "CBS Mornings" on Wednesday. The companies affected by the outages have said they were due to issues such as routine maintenance or upgrades, while the Federal Aviation Administration blamed its nationwide ground stop last week on a contractor updating its flight system."All of them have denied that cyberattacks are to blame," Gutman said. "Still, the system failures are fueling online speculation about a larger cyber threat."Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday that there's "zero evidence" that the recent outages in the U.S. are linked. "The Microsoft incident has nothing to do with what we saw with the FAA. The FAA has nothing to do with what we saw with the banks a few days ago. These issues that we've seen from a technical standpoint are completely unrelated one from another," Rubio said during a news conference in the Philippines. Costco didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.The close timing of the outages highlights the country's increasing reliance on technology, John D'Arcy, a Temple University professor who researches cybersecurity and information technology failures, told CBS News Philadelphia."Our systems are so much more complex and so much more interconnected than they ever have been in the past, that when we just have one failure, the effects are much more dramatic," D'Arcy said.The surge in panic buying could lift Costco's sales, Bellinger wrote. His 31-year-old girlfriend, whom police have only identified by her last name, Arroyo, survived the attack without any serious injuries, police said initially. Police allege he and Arroyo "planned a robbery targeting the American with the intent of obtaining the PINs for bank cards" linked to the hotel.Van Dyke's brother, Peter Van Dyke, told CBS News the revelation that police suspect she was involved in Kurt Van Dyke's death is "shocking."He said the fact that she was found alive following the attack struck him and his family as "extremely odd," but said he "didn't want to make any speculations.""We had our suspicions," he said.Kurt Van Dyke had lived in Costa Rica since the '80s. national.body:
Barbara Ortutay, Associated Press Barbara Ortutay, Associated Press

OAKLAND, Calif. (AP) — Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share on Wednesday, an amount above the expected price range that values the artificial intelligence giant at $1.5 trillion.

The higher-than-anticipated pricing signals broad investor enthusiasm for AI stocks even amid some uncertainty in the market stemming from the ouster of Nvidia's CEO and worries about an AI bubble.

Anthropic said the offering consists of 980 million shares, roughly 956 million sold by the company and the rest by selling stockholders. Proceeds totaling $81 billion put Anthropic's IPO ahead of SpaceX, which raised about $75 billion in June.

The San Francisco-based maker of the Claude AI tool is set to make its debut Thursday on Wall Street. The company had set a price range of $70 to $78 per share, offering 825 million shares that will begin trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "ANT."

Anthropic decided to barrel ahead with the IPO despite jitters among some investors over market volatility, a potential regulatory crackdown by a Democratic-led Congress next year and growing anti-AI sentiment among the public. Then there's the spectacular downfall of one of the industry's biggest cheerleaders, former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, over extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

"This is strong appetite for this major AI IPO in Anthropic, and it's a big win for the tech sector after a white-knuckle time with Nvidia. The pricing shows strong demand among investors," said Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co.

The company's rival, OpenAI, is not planning to go public until next year.

national.summary: Châtaigniers en fleurs was painted in 1890 in the final two months of Vincent van Gogh's life.
national.body:
Auction house Sotheby's has sold a painting by Vincent van Gogh for a record $190.4m (£144.8m).

The sale of Châtaigniers en fleurs ("Chestnut Trees in Blossom") shatters the renowned artist's previous auction record of $117.2 million set in 2022.

The historic sale in New York on Wednesday comes after an eleventh-hour agreement was reached to resolve a dispute regarding claims the art piece was previously sold under duress during the rise of the Nazis.

Châtaigniers en fleurs was painted in 1890 in the final two months of Van Gogh's life. It is considered one of the most important works of art from that period to remain in private hands, according to Sotheby's.

Sotheby's auction of $180m Van Gogh challenged over claims it was 'sold under duress'

Published 4 days ago It was not immediately clear who purchased the painting. The BBC has contacted Sotheby's for comment.

The oil painting, which was estimated to carry a value of $180m (£136m) prior to the sale, was put up for auction as part of a set called the Blaquier-Arrieta Collection.

Sotheby's announced in the hours before the auction that it had resolved a dispute between the Blaquier-Arrieta family and the heirs of the Fischer family - the prior German owners of the work - regarding the sale.

national.summary: A slow-moving storm system dumped heavy rains that prompted an emergency declaration Wednesday in South Florida where the roof of a synagogue collapsed and cars were submerged along roads, authorities said.
national.body:
Cody Jackson, Associated Press Cody Jackson, Associated Press

PLANTATION, Fla. (AP) — A slow-moving storm system dumped heavy rains that prompted an emergency declaration Wednesday in South Florida where the roof of a synagogue collapsed and cars were submerged along roads, authorities said.

On the West Coast, heavy rain and high winds grounded planes at San Francisco's airport, disrupted ferry service and flooded roads in Napa County and other wine country areas north of the city.

Preliminary figures for Florida showed 15.3 inches (39 centimeters) of rain fell in a 24-hour period ending Wednesday in parts of Broward County, the National Weather Service said.

The threat was expected to last through Friday along Florida's Atlantic Coast with additional rainfall amounts of 12 inches (30 centimeters) possible, the weather service said.

The Florida Division of Emergency Management said in an advisory Tuesday night that "potentially catastrophic" amounts of rainfall could cause flash flooding, life-threatening rip tides and expected minor beach erosion due to high surf.

On top of all that, ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday, a low-pressure system is expected to form near the northern Bahamas. It could become a subtropical or tropical storm over parts of the southeast and mid-Atlantic coasts into early next week, according to the National Hurricane Center in Miami.

The natural warming cycle called El Niño has disrupted Florida's typical dry season that runs from October to May, said Alejandra Garcia, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service in Miami. El Niño is "helping bring these low pressure systems down toward the southeastern United States, which in turn is causing these heavy precipitation events," she said.

national.title: India's religious make-up - what a new Pew study says about Hindus and Muslims
national.summary: India will remain predominantly Hindu, though its Muslim population is projected to grow faster, according to a new survey.
national.body:
India will remain overwhelmingly Hindu for decades to come, but its religious composition is projected to shift gradually.

A new study by the Pew Research Center, projecting the world's religious populations to 2070, estimates that Hindus will make up 76% of India's population by then, down from 79% in 2020, while the Muslim share will rise from 15% to 20%.

The shift is rooted largely in differences in age and fertility: Indian Muslims are younger than Hindus and, on average, have more children.

The Pew projections place India at the centre of a wider demographic shift across South Asia.

Pakistan is expected to overtake Indonesia as the country with the world's largest Muslim-majority population, with India moving into second place. Bangladesh, too, is projected to see substantial growth in its Muslim population.

The study projects the religious composition of the world over the next 50-year period, drawing on data from 201 countries and territories, covering virtually the entire global population.

It tracks seven religious groups between 2020 and 2070, assuming recent demographic trends continue. Using census and survey data, it establishes each group's size and age profile in 2020, and factors in differences in fertility and religious switching.

The findings place India at the heart of a changing global religious landscape. The country is expected to have the world's second-largest Muslim population by 2070, after Pakistan, with about 334 million Muslims. Pakistan itself will overtake Indonesia as the country with the largest Muslim population, with an estimated 461 million.

national.title: Iran widens Gulf attacks by targeting U.S. air base in Kuwait and sites in Bahrain
national.summary: Iran said that its recent attacks — including those on other U.S. facilities in Bahrain on Sunday and Friday — were in response to U.S. drone surveillance operations and an attack on Iranian communications towers.
national.body:
David Rising, Associated Press David Rising, Associated Press

Aamer Madhani, Associated Press Aamer Madhani, Associated Press

CAIRO (AP) — Iran widened its attacks on its Gulf neighbors on Wednesday, targeting a U.S. air base in Kuwait and launching several attacks on Bahrain in what appeared to be retaliation for American strikes the day before.

After about two months without such attacks, Iran has repeatedly targeted U.S. facilities in Bahrain in recent days. The small Persian Gulf island kingdom hosts the U.S. Navy's 5th Fleet.

The early morning attacks in the nearly nine-month-old war came after a U.S. fighter jet struck a Revolutionary Guard missile launch site Tuesday on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. strike was in retaliation for an Iranian attack on an American radar installation in Bahrain earlier Tuesday.

Iran said that its recent attacks — including those on other U.S. facilities in Bahrain on Sunday and Friday — were in response to U.S. drone surveillance operations and an attack on Iranian communications towers.

The tit-for-tat attacks come as the commander of the U.S. military's Central Command, Adm. Brad Cooper, met Wednesday in Tel Aviv with Israel's military chief of staff, Eyal Zamir, and the director of Israel's intelligence agency Mossad, Roman Gofman.

They also complicate negotiations for a diplomatic solution and raise the risk of resumption of all-out conflict as a conflict in Yemen between Iran-backed Houthi rebels and a Saudi-led coalition could drag on for months.

national.title: Russian arrested for spying on US defence company Palantir over Ukraine support
national.summary: The suspect followed employees and was found with fake US IDs and two Russian passports, prosecutors say.
national.body:
A Russian man has been arrested in California's Silicon Valley for allegedly attempting to spy on employees of a technology and defence firm that supports the Ukrainian military.

Igor D'iu is accused of acting as an agent of a foreign government to conduct a covert operation in Palo Alto, near San Francisco. The BBC understands that the company targeted was Palantir Technologies.

D'iu is also charged with stalking employees and possessing falsified identity documents.

The company is not named in charging documents, but is described as a publicly traded technology and defence company that produces software used by Ukraine in its war with Russia.

"The allegations in this case describe a state-sponsored operation to target and harass employees of an American technology and defense company because of that company's assistance to Ukraine in its war with Russia," said US Attorney for the Northern District of California Craig Missakian.

"We will not tolerate any efforts - by foreign governments or otherwise - to turn Silicon Valley into a base for foreign intelligence operations."

Prosecutors say that D'iu entered the US unlawfully via the Mexico border, after travelling there from Istanbul in June.

He was allegedly recruited through the Telegram encrypted messaging app. His handlers referred to Russia as "'the Motherland' and directed D'iu to gather information about the company because it was supplying weapons used against Russia in Ukraine".

Nike is gifting high school valedictorians across the country with a pair of custom sneakers after Mississippi's incoming senator appealed to the company on social media.

Scott Colom, who is poised to become the state's first Black U.S. senator since Reconstruction, called on the sneaker giant to honor his historic election by giving every high school valedictorian in his state a pair of custom Air Force 1s -- his favorite style. The sneakers cost between $90 and $180 on the company's web site.

"It would encourage MS students to hit the books the rest of the year! #justdoit," the Democrat suggested Monday on X, referencing Nike's famous slogan.

The company accepted the challenge and took it one step further.

"The athlete mindset makes things possible, including this idea," Oregon-based Nike responded Tuesday on X. "@scott_colom, we'll do you one better… For this year, 2026/2027 high school valedictorians from across the U.S., let's go!"

Nike said more details would be forthcoming, but Colom has already suggested the custom sneaker should give a nod to Hiram Revels, a fellow Mississippian who was the first African American to serve in Congress when he took office in 1870.

national.title: AP report: Bernie Sanders unveils how he'll push for Medicare for All when Democrats take power
national.summary: Sen. Bernie Sanders is preparing to use his return atop a powerful Senate committee to push for sweeping changes to the nation's healthcare system, setting up an early test of how far Democrats are willing to go in embracing progressive priorities.
national.body:
Joey Cappelletti, Associated Press Joey Cappelletti, Associated Press

WASHINGTON (AP) — Sen. Bernie Sanders is preparing to use his return atop a powerful Senate committee to push for sweeping changes to the nation's healthcare system, setting up an early test of how far Democrats are willing to go in embracing progressive priorities.

Sanders, a Vermont independent who caucuses with Democrats, is currently the ranking member on the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee and is expected to become its chairman when Democrats take control of the Senate in January. His agenda, first provided to The Associated Press, lays out the legislative implementation for proposals that he and progressive candidates championed on the campaign trail this cycle.

At the center is Sanders' longstanding push for Medicare for All, a universal healthcare system that would be implemented over four years. The first year would lower the Medicare eligibility age from 65 to 55, expand coverage to include dental, vision and hearing care, and guarantee healthcare to children through age 18.

"This is no longer a utopian vision. This is where the American people are," Sanders said in an interview with the AP.

WATCH: Health care costs a major concern for voters ahead of midterms

The proposals offer an early glimpse of how progressives hope to shape the Democratic Party's priorities after an election that delivered the party control of Congress but also exposed competing visions for its future. With the 2028 presidential election already looming, Sanders is seeking to push Democrats toward a populist economic agenda that he argues has gained broader support.

"I think the election, in my opinion, was a crying out for fundamental change in the way the government does business and the absolute need to protect a struggling working class," Sanders said. "I think this is a time to bring about very significant changes in policies so that we can actually improve the lives of working families."

"Word has gotten around that it's soothing and pleasant for the animals who have to wait here in cages to have some pleasant background music," he said. "So, the call went out to musicians around Rochester to come and lend a hand, and I think a lot of us are excited to do that."

Henne's audience was a roomful of cats. A scared looking red tabby wearing a surgical cone slowly peered over the top of the box he was perched in.

"A little quiet acoustic music maybe is a nice way to let the cats know that we're not threatening and this is a safe place," Henne said, after noticing that the cat, Jack, was frightened.

Music has the power to move us and soothe us and animals are not immune to its magic. That's the philosophy behind Lollypop Farm ' s new venture with Wild Tunes, a Houston-based nonprofit devoted to enriching the lives of homeless pets.

Wild Tunes was founded in 2023 by Yuvi Agarwal, a 10-year-old animal lover and musician who saw how his music calmed his dog.

"Animals who are coming into this space are often dealing with a lot of change, a lot of uncertainty, and that leads to anxiety," noted Sydney Jenkins, Lollypop Farm's director of humane education.

The hope, she said, is that live music will provide relief for the anxiety and a safe, comforting human connection.

local.body:
Rand Aerospace & Defense Group's plans to add a second factory in the southern end of the county are moving ahead.

The Chautauqua County Industrial Development Agency approved financial assistance for a $5.22 million expansion plan for Rand, as it purchases the former Serta Mattress factory in the town of Ellicott.

According to Rosemarie Strandburg with the county IDA, this second location will allow Rand to not only keep its current 115 employees but add an additional 31 employees over the next three years.

Rand currently operates out of 2072 Allen Street Ext. in the town of Ellicott and plans to continue that location as it acquires this new location in Mason Industrial Park.

"This expansion represents an important next chapter for Rand as we continue to grow our capabilities and respond to increasing demand from our customers," Dan McKenrick, president and CEO of Rand Aerospace & Defense Group said in a statement after the meeting. "Our investment in this new facility will provide the additional manufacturing capacity needed to support our existing and future programs, while creating new opportunities for our employees and the local workforce. We are proud to continue investing in Chautauqua County and appreciate the support of the CCIDA and our local partners."

McKenrick first approached the county IDA publicly about Rand purchasing the former Serta Mattress located at 2375 Parkway Drive in October. At that meeting, he credited the county IDA for helping Rand solidify in the past, which is allowing them to be able to expand.

"Supporting the growth of established manufacturers like Rand is a key part of our economic development strategy," said Mark Geise, deputy county executive for economic development and the chief executive officer for the county IDA. "This project represents a significant private-sector investment that will increase manufacturing capacity, retain more than 100 existing jobs, and create additional employment opportunities. By working collaboratively with businesses and our municipal partners, we can help ensure that companies like Rand have the resources and infrastructure they need to continue growing right here in Chautauqua County."

Other officials issued statements praising the IDA Board of Director's decision to support the project.

local.title: State moving forward with nuclear plans
local.summary: New York state Gov. Kathy Hochul has announced the completion of the Master Plan for Responsible Advanced Nuclear Development in New York (Advanced Nuclear Master Plan). Demonstrating New York’s leadership role in the national effort to develop new nuclear energy, the Master Plan is a comprehensive
local.body:
New York state Gov. Kathy Hochul has announced the completion of the Master Plan for Responsible Advanced Nuclear Development in New York (Advanced Nuclear Master Plan). Demonstrating New York's leadership role in the national effort to develop new nuclear energy, the Master Plan is a comprehensive statewide roadmap to achieve the Governor's Nuclear Reliability Backbone to create five gigawatts (GW) of new nuclear power.

Co-authored by the New York State Energy Research Development Authority (NYSERDA) and the New York State Department of Public Service (DPS), and unveiled today at the State's third Nuclear Summit in Rochester, the master plan outlines coordinated state actions to support the safe and timely development and deployment of advanced nuclear power plants in upstate New York.

"Expanding emission-free, round-the-clock nuclear power is a cornerstone of my all-of-the-above approach to ensure we have enough energy to keep the lights on and costs down for New Yorkers," Hochul said. "The completed Advanced Nuclear Master Plan can serve as a national model by pairing our ambitious target of five gigawatts of new nuclear generation with a comprehensive strategy to support thoughtful development and deployment of what will be the largest buildout the country has seen in more than three decades."

Dunkirk's former NRG plant, now owned by Genover, could be a candidate for this type of power generation. It was one of eight communities to express an interest in the opportunity in 2025.

The master plan was developed in response to Hochul's 2025 directive to establish a framework supporting advanced nuclear energy development in New York. Now, the master plan will help facilitate the development of the Nuclear Reliability Backbone, which Governor Hochul directed the creation of in her 2026 State of the State, that will add 5 gigawatts of new nuclear generation to the 3.4 gigawatts already in existence.

DPS today also issued a White Paper with policy recommendations to help enable the commercial viability of advanced nuclear development, potential cost reductions and other considerations for advancing the Governor's Nuclear Reliability Backbone.

In addition, the New York Power Authority (NYPA) also continues to move forward to develop and construct at least one gigawatt of nuclear energy in Upstate New York.

Public Service Commission Chair Rory Christian said, "The Master Plan and White Paper announced today offer actionable next steps to safely and responsibly facilitate the development of 5 gigawatts of new nuclear in New York State. Thanks to the leadership of Governor Hochul, these collaborative and comprehensive interagency workstreams serve as a strong foundation to expand New York's nuclear footprint to maintain a reliable grid while centering community input and workforce opportunities."

Asked Wednesday what gives him hope that his struggling team, which is mired near the bottom of the Eastern Conference and has three regulation wins t
local.body:
CRANBERRY TOWNSHIP, Pa. -- It took Kyle Dubas more than three years, but the Pittsburgh Penguins general manager finally said the quiet part out loud.

Asked Wednesday what gives him hope that his struggling team, which is mired near the bottom of the Eastern Conference and has three regulation wins through 20 games, can turn it around in time to salvage this season, Dubas turned philosophical.

Yes, making the playoffs for a second straight year would be nice. Yet that’s not the metric he will lean on to gauge progress.

Dubas would like the team’s younger players to take “major steps.” He’d like to see the iconic, aging core led by captain Sidney Crosby show it still has “gas left in the tank.” He’d like some of the prospects he’s acquired since taking over to make a push for NHL playing time.

If those things can happen, Dubas believes the franchise will be on “the right track” regardless of where the Penguins wind up in the standings.

Then, Dubas finished by using a phrase that included the one word he has consistently avoided uttering publicly since taking over in the summer of 2023.

“This has been, I think rightfully, an unorthodox style of rebuilding a team because of the players that are here,” he said.

A rebuild that has tried to do two things at once: point toward the future without tarnishing the legacy of Crosby, Evgeni Malkin and Kris Letang.

How else do you describe the massive turnover in both the House of Representatives and U.S. Senate? Democrats last gained nine or more Senate seats in a midterm electio
local.body:
If there is one thing the midterm elections decided nationally, it was this. Americans want a better system of checks and balances.

How else do you describe the massive turnover in both the House of Representatives and U.S. Senate?

Democrats last gained nine or more Senate seats in a midterm election in 1958, during Republican President Dwight Eisenhower's second term. That year, Democrats wrested away 13 Republican-held seats and also won both of Alaska's newly created seats, for a total gain of 15 seats.

Former Rep. Mary Peltola's victory in the controversial Alaska race gave Democrats a 56-44 majority when the new Congress begins in January, marking the party's largest advantage in the Senate in 16 years. Democrats held 58 Senate seats in the waning days of the 111th Congress, which concluded on Jan. 3, 2011.

"Fifty-six seats was an unimaginable result even just a few months ago,” Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer said in a statement posted on social media. “Most people didn't think 51 Democratic Senate seats was a possibility at the beginning of this cycle."

Even without Alaska, Democrats would have secured their largest majority since January 2015, when Republicans took control after flipping nine Democratic seats in the 2014 midterms during President Barack Obama's second term.

As for readers, many in this region who did vote Republican in local elections, 53% in response to our poll question, "Are you pleased with the national election results?" said no while 47% said "yes."

Red & Green junior Beckett Lumia was named the All-Conference Player of the Year, senior Aaden Howard was named the league's Defensive Player of the Year and senior Caden Wahl was Jamestown's Individual Sportsmanship Award winner as the team was also recognized. Junior midfielder Collin Coleman had 16 goals and five assists, freshman midfielder Colten Wilczewski had two goals and an assist, sophomore defender Adam Jaquith had two goals and three assists while anchoring a defense that allowed just 18 goals on the season, and senior goalkeeper Donovan Booker helped the Gators post 11 clean sheets.

Second-place Southwestern had a pair of players recognized on the First Team. Junior forward Wilson Genareo had 16 goals and three assists while junior midfielder Matthew Persia had eight goals and four assists.

Olean had three players honored on the First Team. Senior forward Connor Hogle had 23 goals and three assists, senior midfielder Ethan Woodring had eight assists and junior defender Gehrig Perry anchored a defense that allowed 52 goals against.

Dunkirk senior midfielder Brady Dobek was named the league's Offensive Player of the Year after tallying eight goals and 12 assists. He was joined on the First Team by senior midfielder Lucas Felt, who had six goals and five assists, and junior defender Brendan Worczak, who anchored a defense that allowed 45 goals against.

Allegany-Limestone/Hinsdale had three players named to the Second Team in sophomore forward Owen Buzzard (14 goals, two assists), senior defender Colton Reska and junior defender Hunter Cassidy (one assist).

local.body:
For me, Thanksgiving weekend is the first "gift of the season." Dear Richard and I have spent the past dozen Thanksgivings in Massachusetts with my daughter's family. But this year the tables are turned.

The scattered family members are all coming here, beginning this Sunday. For nine days. Arrivals continue daily until everyone is on hand by Wednesday night for the traditional welcome home supper of homemade corn chowder and biscuits. That supper succeeded 35 years ago because it didn't matter how late arrival time drifted- it would always be ready. Plus, chowder is a warm welcome when you've been on the road. Within those years, the cell phone certainly has helped with ETA's and knowing when to put the biscuits in the oven. The combo became the planned staple when my collegiate daughter commented, "Can we have your chowder when we arrive?" Instant tradition!

Since we won't all be together for the Christmas holiday - first time in seven years - I've decided to combine a little bit of each holiday next week. In an addition to a few yuletide decorations, we're just going to do our traditional Christmas stockings.

We each buy one thing for everyone else's stocking, and they fill up pretty fast. And since there won't be any pile of presents under the tree? I'm skipping the tree.

Meanwhile, I'm planning our usual over-the-top Thanksgiving feast, New England style. Not only are we traditional, but I found out the year that I modified the apple stuffing that tradition is not to be tampered with. Autumn magazines are filled with recipes for newfangled pumpkin pie or adding sausage to the stuffing, but any changes I attempt are always greeted by loud objections. However, in deference to our British son-in-law, Ian, we have added Brussels sprouts to our Yankee menu. I applaud the addition to the other five vegetables.

Early in my life, I was so imbued by the way a "proper" thanksgiving should be celebrated that it never occurred to me anyone did anything differently. I was young and single in San Diego when I received a generous invitation. My friendly hosts had invited me for "Thanksgiving with all the trimmings." Although I was pretty sure there wouldn't be two kinds of Cape Cod cranberry sauce, I arrived with wine and great anticipation. The "trimmings" turned out to be ham, yams, and a broccoli Jello salad. I do remember saying yes to a second margarita. In the end, we did have pumpkin pie - with chocolate chip ice cream. And they had seemed like such nice people.

local.title: ‘No updates, no nothing’: Mourning families demand justice for July 4 murders in Niagara Falls
local.summary: Chants of ‘We want justice’ rang throughout Niagara Falls, as the family and friends of Jayla Brown and Jalin Rios demanded answers as to why nobody has been arrested for killing their loved ones.
local.body: Chants of ‘We want justice’ rang throughout Niagara Falls, as the family and friends of Jayla Brown and Jalin Rios demanded answers as to why nobody has been arrested for killing their loved ones.It has been over four months since 19-year-old Jayla Brown and 22-year-old Jalin Rios were shot and killed at Fourth of July gatherings in Niagara Falls.The two were killed in separate shootings on the same day. Their mothers, Carretha Brown and Celis Rios, say the lack of an arrest by the Niagara Falls Police Department has only angered the families and added to their grief.“We lost our son, and nobody has been accountable for his death,” Celis said.“We need answers. We want everything to come out right now,” Jalin’s dad Jason said.“Absolutely hell. No one contacts me, no updates, no nothing. If I don't reach out, I don't hear from anyone,” Brown said. We need answers for these unsolved murders, these homicides. We need answers, and we need them to be more diligent about solving these murders.”Together, the Rios and Brown families led a march of a few hundred people down Main Street, from the Niagara Falls Police Department to City Hall.The group carried pictures and signs of both Jalin and Jayla, and they chanted ‘We want justice’ for not just their own loved ones, but for all those killed in Niagara Falls, who have seen their investigations go cold.“They keep saying the same thing. We're waiting, we're waiting, we're waiting. We're tired of waiting. We want action,” Celis said.“We're going to keep on stomping. Yes, we're boots on the ground,” Brown said. “We're not politicians, but we're soldiers, and we're not stopping until we get some things accomplished because it's just time.”Brown told me that along with justice for their children, she’s asking the city to invest more in public infrastructure for the city’s youth to participate in. entertainment.summary: Ella Langley dominated the awards ceremony, as the winner of entertainer of the year, the biggest award of the night.
entertainment.body:
The 60th annual Country Music Association Awards took place live from Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena on Wednesday night.

Ella Langley dominated the awards ceremony, as the winner of entertainer of the year, the biggest award of the night.

While accepting the award, she joked that the crowd must be sick of her already, getting a laugh from those in the room.

“This isn’t real life,” she said while accepting the award. “Thank you Jesus, I’m at a loss for words,” she added, before saying, “This has been the most special night.

As she swept all the categories she was nominated in, Lainey Wilson brought out a bedazzled broom for her, telling her she knew she had it prepared as she knew Langley was going to sweep the show.

Langley also won music video of the year before the broadcast.

“Choosin’ Texas” was named as the music video of the year winner during Good Morning America Wednesday morning.

The record-breaking hit, also won single of the year and song of the year.

entertainment.title: Pierce Brosnan Welcomes Robert Pattinson Into James Bond Role: ‘Enjoy the Ride’
entertainment.summary: The actors notably worked together in 2010 on the film Remember Me
entertainment.body:
Former 007 Pierce Brosnan has officially welcomed Robert Pattinson into the James Bond club . The actor, who play the spy in four films from 1995-2002, shared a photo of Pattison on Instagram along with a personal message for his former co-star from 2010 romantic drama Remember Me .

“Dear Robert, Welcome to the world of Bond,” Brosnan wrote. “You are going to be magnificent. I have fond memories of our time together making ‘Remember Me.’ It has been a joy to watch you create a remarkable body of work and to go from strength to strength. Enjoy the ride. Grá mor, Pierce.”

Brosnan is not the first former Bond to congratulate Pattinson. George Lazenby, who played Bond in 1969’s On Her Majesty’s Secret Service , also reminded the Batman actor, “Remember to enjoy yourself.”

“I hear they’ve announced the new James Bond @007,” Lazenby wrote on X . “Robert, welcome to the most exclusive club in the world. But remember to enjoy yourself. Let’s see if you’ll have ‘this never happened to the other fella’ moment. All the best mate, George.”

entertainment.title: Larry Poindexter, ‘S.W.A.T.’ and ‘Days of Our Lives’ actor, dead at 66 after being hit by car
entertainment.summary: Actor Larry Poindexter, known for "S.W.A.T." and "Days of Our Lives," died at 66 days after being struck by a car in Los Angeles.
entertainment.body:
Larry Poindexter, the soap opera veteran known for his roles on “Days of Our Lives” and “General Hospital,” has died days after he was struck by a car in Los Angeles. He was 66.

Poindexter died suddenly Wednesday morning, Deadline reported .

The “S.W.A.T.” actor was hit while crossing the street on his way to pick up food in Studio City, Calif., where he lived, on Nov. 11.

Poindexter had been hospitalized as he was awaiting surgery for his broken ribs before his death.

Page Six has reached out to Poindexter’s representatives for comment.

Poindexter, whose Hollywood career spanned more than four decades and nearly 200 film and television credits, was born in Dallas in 1959 to Tony Award-winning lighting and set designer H.R. Poindexter and opera singer Sue Ann Erdman, according to his IMDb page .

Long before his TV career took off, the “Days of Our Lives” alum was a college stage performer, taking on musicals and plays in Texas and Ohio.

He eventually moved to Los Angeles, where he worked as an actor and production coordinator with producer Franklin R. Levy and his Catalina Production Group.

entertainment.title: Tom Busby’s ‘Rockhampton Hangover’ Named 2026 Queensland Album of the Year
entertainment.summary: Busby beat out a shortlist of albums from the likes of Clea, Radium Dolls, Platonic Sex, 2 Charm and The Jungle Giants.
entertainment.body:
Tom Busby collects The Triffid’s 2026 Queensland Album of the Year with his debut solo longplay, Rockhampton Hangover .

The Rockhampton-raised singer and songwriter, Busby, one-half of the chart-topping blues and roots duo Busby Marou , beat out a shortlist of albums from the likes of Clea, Radium Dolls, Platonic Sex, 2 Charm and The Jungle Giants.

Now in its 11 th year, the public-voted award celebrates Queensland’s music community and was presented at Brisbane live music spot The Triffid, part of the Live Nation portfolio of venues. Produced by Ben Kweller and recorded in the Texas Hill Country, the album is a meditation on family, home and finding your way through change.

“I’m pretty bloody stoked,” Busby says of his award. “It took me a long time to get around to making a solo record, and when I finally did, I kept coming back to stories from home. To have The Triffid name Rockhampton Hangover Album of the Year means a lot. Big thanks to Ben Kweller for making it with me, to everyone who’s given it a spin and to The Triffid crew for backing Queensland music.”

“Tom has given so much to Queensland music through Busby Marou, so it’s great to see him take this step and have people really connect with the record,” adds John Collins, co-founder of The Triffid and bass player with Powderfinger , which is reuniting in 2027 for what promises to be one of the year’s biggest tours down under.

“Making your first solo album is a big thing,” he continues. “Having the fans vote it their favorite makes it even sweeter.”

The award was created to bring attention to music from Australia’s Sunshine State, explains Collins, and for sparking conversations about the artists making it.

entertainment.title: ‘The Altruists’ Review: Anthony Boyle and Julia Garner Make a Toxically Perfect Match in Netflix’s Intriguing but Unsatisfying Crypto Love Story
entertainment.summary: Based on the real-life rise and fall of FTX, the eight-part miniseries from Graham Moore ('The Imitation Game') delves into the romance between founder Sam Bankman-Fried and exec Caroline Ellison.
entertainment.body:
As FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried ( Anthony Boyle ) begins his very public downfall, one salacious detail starts to go viral: That Caroline Ellison ( Julia Garner ), CEO of sister firm Alameda and his ex-girlfriend, was a prolific writer of smutty Harry Potter fanfiction.

The fact that her private hobby has nothing to do with the financial crimes they’re in hot water for is beside the point. “What gets more clicks than a complicated financial scandal? A young professional woman who’s into kink,” shrugs Constance (Madison Hu), FTX’s loyal-to-the-end COO. “I mean, that’s the story. The whole world didn’t care about Caroline until they realized that she was horny.” Related Stories TV Netflix's New Releases Coming in November 2026 TV 'The Altruists': Anthony Boyle's Sam Bankman-Fried Caught in Crypto Crisis in Netflix Series Trailer The Altruists The Bottom Line All heart and not enough head. Airdate: Thursday, Nov. 19 (Netflix) Cast: Julia Garner, Anthony Boyle, Alex Lawther, Karan Soni, Madison Hu, Eugene Young, Naomi Okada, Matt Rife, Robin Weigert, Paul Reiser, Terry Chen Creator: Graham Moore

Sam, who knows better than anyone how mortified Caroline must be, seems troubled by the notion. But it more or less appears to be the impulse driving Netflix’s The Altruists . The eight-hour series chronicles the rise and fall of FTX and Alameda through the tumultuous relationship between its leaders — and in doing so, deepens the saga’s emotional relatability while also diminishing its stakes.

For most of the season, creator Graham Moore ( The Imitation Game ) cuts between two timelines. In the halcyon days of 2016, captured by director James Ponsoldt in the warm bright tones and slightly grainy texture of an indie rom-com, Caroline meets Sam on her first day at a New York hedge fund. The two recognize each other almost immediately as kindred spirits, matched in their intelligence (high), their interests (math and winning) and their taste in jokes (charmingly dorky).

In no time, they’re falling into bed, though not quite into a relationship — Caroline prefers to keep it caszh, reasoning that non-monogamy is more “mathematically optimal” for getting off. Instead, they tie their fates together via their careers. Sam first founds Alameda and then FTX, and in short order brings Caroline on board as an exec.

The businesses are rooted in the couple’s shared principle of effective altruism. In theory, EA is a rationalist moral framework that prioritizes doing the greatest good. In practice, like most guiding philosophies, it’s easily twisted into whatever a self-interested devotee wants it to be.

entertainment.title: CISAC’s International Standard Musical Work Codes System Hits 100 Million Songs Milestone
entertainment.summary: The system, which assigned its first code to ABBA's "Dancing Queen" 30 years ago, has been instrumental in helping songwriters get paid.
entertainment.body:
CISAC (the International Confederation of Societies of Authors and Composers) says its International Standard Musical Work Codes system — the tracking mechanism it created to identify and track individual songs — has hit the 100 million songs milestone.

“Behind every code is a song, a story, and the people who created it, CISAC’s director of business and technology said in a statement. “CISAC’s priority is to strengthen the connection between accurate data and fair remuneration for the creators the system serves.”

The first work assigned an ISWC code, or T-000.000.001.0, was ABBA’s “Dancing Queen” 30 years ago.

The code is an essential ingredient in ensuring songwriters get paid, especially in today’s world, where multiple collection societies around the globe track activity for each song, many of which have multiple songwriters. Each code provides a unique, permanent reference for a musical work, connecting it to information about its authors and composers, the announcement says, adding it has become key in sharing musical works data across the global network of song collection management organizations, also known as performance rights organizations in the U.S. Today, more than 100 societies around the globe are using the new system.

CISAC adds that close to 30 publishers are allocating ISWCs by themselves and validating those ISWCs against the database. It says the major digital service providers (DSPs) and data companies have started to query the ISWC system, resulting in more than 20 million queries per month.

CISAC notes that it completed a “major modernization of the ISWC system in 2020… in order to improve speed, accuracy and efficiency of code assignment,” facilitating song activity and the subsequent responsibility of paying royalties to the rightful parties.

“Founded in Paris in 1926, [CISAC] continues to develop the international cooperation, standards and systems that help creators benefit from the use of their works as technology evolves,” added the organization in a statement.

During the Nov. 19 episode of The Kardashians , Lamar Odom was seen addressing the public response to his 2026 documentary , noting that when it came to their marriage, his overdose and their subsequent divorce that he hoped his ex Khloe had “healed by now.”

“I’m sorry the fact that he’s doing interviews being so angry towards me, are you f--king well? I know you’re not,” she told sister Kim Kardashian . “Anyone that was around saw what was going on and then you played me. Even the fact that in the documentary, they were not even nice about me. Everyone can f--k off.”

The Good American founder—who previously said her ex was “dead” to her after the release of his documentary—went on to note “everyone is a pathological liar.”

“All those years that I thought we were in love,” Khloe added, “and we had all this great stuff.”

However, when Kim shared that Lamar may have just been in love with the idea of being with Khloe, she couldn’t help but agree.

“I was used,” Khloe said. “But it was real for me. And that’s what hurts my heart so badly. Seeing how bamboozled I been, you think I care to trust any male ever in my life again? F--k no. Everyone can suck my f--king d--k.”

In Netflix’s Untold: The Death & Life of Lamar Odom , Lamar—who wed Khloe in 2009—alleged the basis of their marriage was to push his own name forward, minimizing the role she played in helping him recover after his near-fatal 2015 overdose.

It’s an end result that Kim still can’t believe. “I didn’t realize how much he used you,” Kim explained to Khloe, “until I saw that documentary.”

entertainment.summary: The popular 2000s shoe line gets its global re-launch on Friday, Nov. 20.
entertainment.body:
Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson ‘s reboot with Reebok is making a comeback, just in time for Christmas.

The hip-hop veteran recently teamed up with the sportswear specialist for the G-Unit G6, a blast from the past sneaker which were unveiled in August in its original red, white and blue colorway and proved to be a hit with 50 Cent’s followers. Those shoes re-launch globally on Friday, Nov. 20 .

The basketball and street fashion-inspired gear initially rolled out in 2003, the year when Fifty blew up on airwaves and charts around the globe. The one that got away, “In Da Club,” logged nine weeks at No. 1 on the Hot 100, and the New Yorker followed it up two months later with “21 Questions,” featuring the late Nate Dogg, which spent a full month atop the national singles survey. His smash album Get Rich or Die Tryin’ held the top spot on the Billboard 200 for six weeks, and lent its name to the 2005 semi-autobiographical film, which gave 50 Cent his first starring role. Related Underscores Is First Transgender Woman Nominated for Best Dance/Electronic Recording Grammy Ella Langley Becomes First Act to Earn Top Two of TouchTunes Frontline Chart El Coyote Earns Third Regional Mexican Airplay No. 1 With 'Ranchero Enamorado' Explore 50 Cent See latest videos, charts and news

That partnership made Jackson one of the first musicians to lead a major footwear franchise. “Creating it the first time was special,” Jackson recounts in an interview with GQ . “I worked with Todd (Krinsky) and the team on everything and they really let me make it mine. It wasn’t just a sneaker—it became part of the culture.”

Krinsky, who started with Reebok in 1993, working in the mailroom, is now CEO. “Our relationship with 50 has always gone beyond sneakers,” he remarks in a statement. “He helped define an important chapter in Reebok’s history, and together we created something that had a lasting impact on sport style and culture. Bringing the G-Unit G6 back is an opportunity to celebrate that legacy while introducing it to a new generation.”

Tastes changed and by 2006 that original partnership had moved, with over four million pairs sold in those three years. Nostalgia and licensed kit, however, make for a powerful combination. “We’ve been talking about it for a while,” 50 continues. “Reebok is back, the G-Unit fans are still here, and there’s a whole new generation discovering us. The timing just felt right.”

entertainment.title: “Wicker Nipples” and All: ‘Wicker’ Cinematographer Celebrates Steamy Film’s Viral Success
entertainment.summary: "Now I know what 'wicker nipples' is in Polish," Lol Crawley quipped at Camerimage about the film that stars Olivia Colman and Alexander Skarsgard.
entertainment.body:
Wicker ‘ s filmmaking team is relishing its viral moments and box office success — not to mention its horny memes .

During a screening of Wicker at Toruń Camerimage Film Festival in Poland on Thursday, cinematographer Lol Crawley introduced the movie and expressed appreciation for it having become a social media sensation. Olivia Colman stars in directors Eleanor Wilson and Alex Huston Fischer’s romantic fantasy as a lonely woman who commissions a basket weaver (Peter Dinklage) to create a husband ( Alexander Skarsgard ) for her. Related Stories Movies Indigenous Queer Drama 'Princess' Is Dedicated to "Everyone Fighting for Their Freedom, Their Identity" Movies 'Sentimental Value' Casting Guru Recalls Meta Stellan Skarsgard and Elle Fanning Experience

“It’s my fourth time back at the festival and having the honor of screening a film in competition, so thank you so much to Camerimage,” Crawley said from the stage about the festival that honors cinematography . “I really do hope you enjoy it as much as we enjoyed making it.”

Crawley went on to recount the movie’s unlikely path from the festival circuit to internet obsession: “The film premiered at Sundance in January of this year, and since the trailer came out and thanks to all the love on social media, it’s just kind of snowballed. It’s gone from its premiere to wicker nipples being available and cardboard cutouts of Alex [Skarsgard] in all his fine wicker glory.”

Wicker has managed to heat things up since Black Bear released it theatrically on Oct. 23. With the makings of a sleeper hit, the film has grossed $23.7 million domestically and an additional $13.4 million internationally through Tuesday. In his review for The Hollywood Reporter , critic Richard Lawson noted its “winning mix of irreverence and compassion.”

The cinematographer acknowledged that the project, notable for its comedic moments, has a bit of a different tone than his previous work. Crawley won Camerimage’s coveted Golden Frog in 2024 for lensing The Brutalist before going on to win the Academy Award for the film.

“It’s a fantastic dark fable — quite different material for me,” Crawley added of Wicker . “But very, very enjoyable experience and very, very proud to present the film.”

Later, after a festival representative had finished translating Crawley’s speech into Polish for the crowd, the Wicker cinematographer quipped, “Now I know what ‘wicker nipples’ is in Polish, which is a takeaway for me.”

entertainment.title: Indigenous Queer Drama ‘Princess’ Is Dedicated to “Everyone Fighting for Their Freedom, Their Identity”
entertainment.summary: Ecuadorian writer-director Christian Rojas' feature debut, which just premiered at Tallinn, is a contribution to the collective healing of wounds, both the creative's own and other people's.
entertainment.body:
Princess , or Ñusta in the Andean indigenous language Quechua, is not your standard coming-of-age film. At the heart of Ecuadorian writer-director Christian Rojas’ lyrical debut feature is Kallpa, 12, who has a big dream: to be chosen as Ñusta, the princess in the teenager’s Andean community’s Winter Solstice Festival. But having been born in the body of a boy, Kallpa is barred from taking part. Rigid tradition and community rejection mean that Kallpa must find a new home and family among a group of local trans women.

Kuri Fuerez stars alongside La Bruja de Texcoco, Bruno Giganti, Quispe Nuna, Romel Vargas, Kayita Quizhpe and Adele Pesantez. Princess , which is a co-production between Ecuador, Mexico, Argentina, Peru and Bolivia, features cinematography by Christian Hidalgo and editing by Jorge Macaya and Cristian Bermeo. The producers are María Ángeles Palacios and Daniela Fuentes Moncada. MMM Film Sales is handling sales. Related Stories Movies 'Sentimental Value' Casting Guru Recalls Meta Stellan Skarsgard and Elle Fanning Experience Movies Sarah Has 'One Month' to Leave Her Parents' Home. She's 45. (Exclusive Clip, Director Chat)

Princess , featuring dialogue in Spanish and Quechua, just celebrated its world premiere in the First Feature Competition of the 30th edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF) in Estonia.

After the premiere screening, Rojas and members of the production and creative team discussed Princess with the audience.

“ Ñusta was born when I was 10 years old, after I had experienced sexual abuse that [affected] my childhood and my life for a long time,” Rojas shared. “I dedicate this film to those who have survived, to those who are still fighting, and to those who open their eyes every day [with] the strength to keep on [being] who they are – everyone fighting for their freedom, their identity, and their right to a life without fear.” Rojas lauded his collaborators as “the best team I could ever have,” concluding: “I say thank you to everyone for being part of it, part of healing this wound collectively – and not just my wound, but those wounds of everyone who’s still fighting and thinks they’re alone. We have to resist, raise our voice, and hug each other as a family.”

Safeguarding and ensuring a safe space, especially for the young actors, was a core focus for the Princess team. “The indigenous families … knew the story from beginning to end, but not the children,” Rojas said. “We had a psychologist on set and in pre-production, trying to develop this secure place for everyone so that we could actually enjoy making this movie.”

entertainment.title: Stephen Baldwin slams brother Alec’s acting chops: ‘Not the most talented’
entertainment.summary: The star unleashed on his older brother’s acting chops, saying he outperformed him in an Oscar-winning movie back in 1995.
entertainment.body:
Actor Stephen Baldwin has come out swinging against his brother Alec Baldwin’s acting skills, saying he is “not the most talented” in the family despite being the “reigning king” financially.

Stephen – who is one of four actor brothers in the famous Baldwin family alongside Alec, Billy and Daniel – spoke of his sibling’s on-screen chops in a recent appearance on the “Still Here Hollywood” podcast.

“He’s not the most talented,” Stephen said of Alec’s ability compared to his brothers. “I’m the only one in a double Oscar-winning film. I gotta rub that in a little bit.”

The film Stephen was referring to is “The Usual Suspects,” in which he starred as career criminal Michael McManus opposite Kevin Spacey.

The film took home an Academy Award for Best Screenplay, with Spacey also winning in the Best Supporting Actor category.

Stephen’s claim appeared to be more of a playful jab than a fact, since both Alec and Billy have appeared in multiple films that have won two or more Oscars, including “The Departed,” “The Aviator” and “Born on the Fourth of July.”

What Alec supposedly lacks in talent, he apparently makes up for in “cash,” according to Stephen.

“Cash is king, so Alec has always kind of been the reigning king, so to speak,” Stephen said of his brother’s Hollywood earnings.

entertainment.title: ‘Never Go Backwards, Just Make Things Bigger and Better’: How Paul O’Neill Chartered Trans-Siberian Orchestra’s Journey Ahead
entertainment.summary: "Paul left us a huge body of unfinished work we need to get to," says Al Pitrelli, TSO's musical director.
entertainment.body:
When Trans-Siberian Orchestra turned 20 back in 2016, the troupe’s enduring success was as surprising to founder Paul O’Neill as anyone in or outside of the camp.

“I would love to say that we planned for it to resonate like this, but it was just pure luck,” acknowledged O’Neill, who passed away the following year at the age of 61 . And that it was an endeavor almost entirely based around the Christmas holiday made it seem even less likely. Related Underscores Is First Transgender Woman Nominated for Best Dance/Electronic Recording Grammy Ella Langley Becomes First Act to Earn Top Two of TouchTunes Frontline Chart El Coyote Earns Third Regional Mexican Airplay No. 1 With 'Ranchero Enamorado' Explore Trans-Siberian Orchestra See latest videos, charts and news

“Normally you have five or six other platinum albums, then you take on Christmas,” O’Neill noted. “Of course, we took it on first and the rest of the year on later. It’s all worked out.”

That’s certainly an understatement for TSO, which celebrates the 30th anniversary of its triple-platinum debut album, Christmas Eve and Other Stories , this year with its annual, two-company concert tour opening Nov. 19 in Green Bay, Wisc., and Council Bluffs, Iowa. The 97 performances through Dec. 30 will again feature the soundtrack and narration from The Ghosts of Christmas Eve , TSO’s 1999 made-for-TV film, and other material amidst the usual fusillade of arena-filling special effects and pyrotechnics, with two shows a day at most stops.

During the past three decades TSO has released six studio albums — four platinum or better, three Christmas-themed — and an EP, along with the multi-platinum singles “Christmas Eve/Sarajevo 12/24” and “Christmas Cannon.” The 2005 track “Wizards in Winter” also hit platinum, and a fan’s synchronized home display soundtracked by the tune was turned into an ad campaign for Miller Lite.

Since 1999, meanwhile, the tours have sold more than 20 million tickets, grossing more than $1 billion. This year, too, TSO will continue its practice of donating $1 from each ticket sold to local charities.

“One of the first things Paul taught us was, ‘Listen, just try to make great art, try to make the best of this as we can, and with a little bit of luck everything will fall into place,'” Al Pitrelli, TSO’s musical director and guitarist with the West company, tells Billboard via phone. “Boy, those words come true every time we hit the stage. His integrity and work ethic carried us through 21 years of touring and 25 years of recording, and with his family at the helm and everybody’s dedication to this, there’s really no end in sight.”

entertainment.summary: Former singer Stefanie Fair reached a $70,000 settlement with the Tennessee Highway Patrol following a wrongful DUI arrest while sober.
entertainment.body:
Wild Orchid singer Stefanie Fair was awarded $70,000 after Tennessee Highway Patrol troopers wrongfully arrested and charged the pop star for DUI — while she was stone-cold sober.

Fair, 53, who sang alongside Fergie in the ’90s girl group, is expected to receive the payout within the next few weeks as the Tennessee Board of Claims approved the settlement over the June 2024 incident, a spokesman for the state attorney general’s office told WSMV4, which first reported the deal Tuesday.

Fair was pulled over by THP Trooper Keith Velez for failing to change lanes while driving in Nashville, WSMV4 reported .

Velez claimed he detected a “very distinct odor of alcohol that comes from either the person or inside the vehicle,” though Fair told him she didn’t drink, body-cam footage obtained by the outlet shows.

“She almost f–king hit me when I was wrapping up a traffic stop,” Velez can be heard telling another trooper who arrived at the scene. “I just come up to the car, and it just reeks of alcohol.”

Fair apologized for not moving over, but appeared baffled when Velez claimed he smelled alcohol.

The singer, who also starred in the Bravo reality series “There Goes the Motherhood” and is married to former A&M Records president Ron Fair, was given a field sobriety test and continued to insist she hadn’t had anything to drink.

Velez claimed the test showed she exhibited signs of intoxication. He then arrested her for DUI.

entertainment.title: 2026 CMA Awards Performances, Ranked
entertainment.summary: As Ella Langley dominated the CMA Awards' winners circle, Billboard looks at the night's performances.
entertainment.body:
The night belonged to Ella Langley at Wednesday evening’s (Nov. 18) CMA Awards . Propelled by the success of “Choosin’ Texas,” her album Dandelion and a headlining tour, Langley won her first entertainer of the year honor. She also won female vocalist of the year, single, song and music video of the year (all for “Choosin’ Texas”) and picked up album of the year, for Dandelion .

“I have watched these awards since I was a little kid, and the award I cared most about was song of the year and entertainer of the year,” Langley said in accepting the CMA entertainer of the year honor, adding, “[there] hasn’t been a song on the radio or in my ears at all where I wasn’t imagining what that song would sound like in front of a crowd…”

Other winners during the night included Chris Stapleton, Stephen Wilson Jr., Brooks & Dunn, The Red Clay Strays and the song “McArthur,” from HARDY, Morgan Wallen, Eric Church and Tim McGraw. Lainey Wilson, hosting for a third time, opened the show by paying tribute to the late music legend Dolly Parton.

“Dolly gave us hope, Dolly gave us joy, Dolly gave us her heart,” Wilson said.

Wilson was joined at times to host by Luke Bryan, and also Brad Paisley, in a throwback to the decade-plus that Paisley and Carrie Underwood hosted the CMAs. From there, the evening celebrated the CMA Awards’ six decades of helping to showcase artists on one of country music’s biggest stages.

The evening both celebrated newcomers and established artists, while honoring legendary artists, such as attendees Sammy Kershaw, Randy Travis, Clint Black and Bill Anderson. While Langley dominated the awards wins, the night was filled with an array of performances. Taylor Swift made her first CMA Awards performance in 13 years, and turned it into an entertaining spectacle. Langley performed twice (including a collab with Miranda Lambert), while Wilson Jr. teamed with Chris Stapleton, Zach Top welcomed Dierks Bentley to pay tribute to John Anderson, and more artists shone during their time in CMA Awards spotlight.

The evening was filled with top-notch performances, including heartfelt tributes, unique artist pairings, rollicking new song debuts and of course, a few surprises.
