entertainment.title: John Christ, Guitarist With Danzig, Dies at 61
entertainment.summary: "He was an impressively brilliant guitarist and a wonderfully kind man," reads a tribute from Soundgarden.
entertainment.body:
John Christ , the veteran electric guitarist who wielded the axe for Danzig and Samhain and was widely recognized by the metal community as one of the best to do it, has passed away following a battle with poor health. He was 61. Explore Billboard Danzig See latest videos, charts and news

“It is with a heavy heart that we must inform you of the peaceful passing of John Christ on November 15, 2026,” reads a statement posted on Danzig’s socials. Related Underscores Is First Transgender Woman Nominated for Best Dance/Electronic Recording Grammy Ella Langley Becomes First Act to Earn Top Two of TouchTunes Frontline Chart El Coyote Earns Third Regional Mexican Airplay No. 1 With 'Ranchero Enamorado'

“No services are planned and we kindly ask everyone to respect the family’s privacy during this time,” the post continues. “John loved each and every one of you.”

Born John Wolfgang Knoll, in Baltimore, Maryland, the youngest and only boy of five kids, the future rocker got a relatively traditional music education, initially on the piano before picking up the acoustic guitar, and then plugged in at age 13. Both his parents were accomplished musicians.

In the late ‘80s he dropped out of college, relocated to New Jersey and joined forces with ex- Misfits frontman Glenn Danzig on the black-as-night rock band Samhain , which would later become Danzig. Christ auditioned for the spot, and caught the attention of Danzig and Rick Rubin, who was scouting acts for his record label, Def Jam Recordings, with a performance that was both brutal and bloody, thanks to strumming finger gashed on the strings.

The anecdote is retold on Christ’s biography . “Accidentally brushing up against Glenn, he left five bloody lines on his shoulder. Rubin thought this was awesome—Danzig did not agree—he thought Christ was on speed,” it reads. When he didn’t receive an immediate callback, he pushed the process by leaving guitar riffs on Danzig’s answering machine. It was the stuff Danzig couldn’t ignore.

Christ would often catch the attention with his playing, his bluesy hard-rock sound with frequent pinch harmonics earning him a spot in Guitar World’s list of “The 100 Greatest Metal Guitarists,” coming in at No. 63.

As a member of Danzig from 1987 to 1995, Christ worked on four studio albums and one EP— Danzig (1988), Danzig II: Lucifuge (1990), Danzig III: How the Gods Kill (1992), Thrall-Demonsweatlive (1993), Danzig 4P (1994), and featured on Live on the Black Hand Side (2001) and The Lost Tracks of Danzig (2007). Christ and Danzig graced the charts with “Mother,” which peaked at No. 43 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1994, and with a string of albums. All told, 14 Danzig titles have impacted the Billboard 200, including a best of No. 24 for Danzig III: How The Gods Kill .

entertainment.title: The Biggest Snubs & Surprises at the 2026 CMA Awards
entertainment.summary: The pundits didn't guess every category correctly.
entertainment.body:
Everyone expected Ella Langley to sweep the 2026 CMA Awards , and sure enough, she did, setting a new, all-time record of six awards in one night. That broke the old record of five awards in one night first set by Johnny Cash in 1969 and then tied by Vince Gill in 1993, Alan Jackson in 2002 and Lainey Wilson in 2023.

But that doesn’t mean there were no snubs or surprises at the awards show, which was held at Bridgestone Arena in Nashville on Wednesday (Nov. 18) and hosted by Wilson for the third year in a row (second year in a row as solo host).

The show opened with a tribute to Dolly Parton, who died in August, with Vince Gill and Wilson singing the country icon’s 1974 classic “I Will Always Love You.” There was also a tribute to John Anderson, who died in October, with Dierks Bentley and Zach Top singing his 1983 hit “Swingin.’”

Perhaps because it was the show’s 60th anniversary, there were several backward-looking performances. Taylor Swift included a bit of her 2007 hit “Our Song” (her first No. 1 hit on Billboard ’s Hot Country Songs chart) in her performance of her current hit “I Knew It, I Knew You.” Tim McGraw performed his 1994 hit “Don’t Take the Girl” ( his first No. 1 on Hot Country Songs). Tucker Wetmore performed Hank Williams Jr.’s 1984 hit “All My Rowdy Friends Are Coming Over Tonight.” Brooks & Dunn performed a hit medley.

But let’s get back to what you came for: Here are snubs and surprises from the 2026 CMA Awards.

Musgraves went 0-5 on the night. She had more nominations without a win than anyone else this year. Musgraves hasn’t won a CMA Award since 2019. But she and Lambert teamed for a winning performance on their song “Horses and Divorces,” about two people who managed to mend a fractured friendship.

entertainment.title: Ella Langley & More Record-Setters at the 2026 CMA Awards
entertainment.summary: Ella didn't win everything. It just seemed like it.
entertainment.body:
Ella Langley set a new, all-time record for most CMA Awards wins in one night on Wednesday (Nov. 18). Langley won six awards, breaking the old record of five wins in one night first set by Johnny Cash in 1969 and then tied by Vince Gill in 1993, Alan Jackson in 2002 and Lainey Wilson in 2023.

Langley has won 10 CMA Awards in just three years. Only two other female solo artists and one all-female group have won 10 or more CMA Awards. Miranda Lambert upped her total of wins to 17 this year. Wilson has won 12 (though she didn’t add to her tally this year). The Chicks have won 10.

Langley, 27, became the second-youngest entertainer of the year winner in CMA history. Taylor Swift was even younger, 19, when she won in that category for the first time in 2009. (She was 21 when she won for a second time two years later.)

Langley won entertainer one year after Wilson won in the category for a second time. This is the second time in CMA history that female acts (solo artists or all-female groups) have won back-to-back awards in this category. The first was when Shania Twain won in 1999, followed by The Chicks in 2000.

Langley won single, song and video of the year for her smash “Choosin’ Texas.” She won in all three categories last year in tandem with Riley Green for their sexy duet “You Look Like You Love Me.” She’s the first artist to achieve this three-award sweep twice. The Brooks & Dunn classic “Believe” won all three awards in 2006.

Langley is just the second artist in CMA history to win single of the year two years running. Lady A, then known as Lady Antebellum, won in 2009 with “I Run to You” and in 2010 with “Need You Now.” (“Need You Now” went on to win Grammys for record and song of the year — and no one would be surprised if “Choosin’ Texas” did the same at the 69th annual Grammy Awards next Feb. 7.)

In the CMA competition for song of the year, Langley is the first songwriter to win back-to-back awards since Lori McKenna, who won in 2015 for co-writing “Girl Crush” and in 2016 for writing “Humble and Kind.”

Just two other songwriters (or teams of songwriters) have won song of the year in back-to-back years with different songs. Vince Gill won three years in a row, 1991-93, for co-writing “When I Call Your Name,” “Look at Us” and “I Still Believe in You.” Paul Overstreet and Don Schlitz won in 1986 and 1987 for co-writing “On the Other Hand” and “Forever and Ever, Amen.”

entertainment.body:
The Wheel of Fortune host revealed that he’s taken a new hobby to keep him active in his 51st year of life: yoga. He even put some of his new moves on display for costar Vanna White on the Nov. 18 episode after she suggested, "Show me something."

"I'm not so good. I just started," Seacrest confessed. "But I have this mat in the office upstairs. Between our meetings, I like to get down and do some things."

The American Idol star wasn't afraid to wrinkle his sleek blue ensemble as he dropped into cobra pose, supporting his torso with his arms while curving his back. He then shifted into the pigeon position, where one leg bends toward the chest while the other extends long to bring relief to the hips.

And the burgeoning yogi shared that his inspiration for taking up the wellness activity was to maintain his mobility as he gets older. In other words, "I feel like it's important that at my age, I try and stretch it out."

Still, the radio DJ's enthusiasm for learning yoga hasn't turned him into an expert just yet.

"This is my cobra," Seacrest narrated his flow while quipping, "This is my other insect. I'm not quite sure the names of them yet."

To that end, after his humble tutorial for White, he had no choice but to divulge, "I've only done it twice," while also teasing his next spiritual pastime: "I'm taking up sound bowls next."

And it's been a year of firsts for Seacrest, who also recently received his very first airbrush tan .

entertainment.title: Summer Walker Files $20 Million Cross-Complaint Against Interscope
entertainment.summary: The move follows after the label sued Walker first, saying she would owe $50 million if she walked away from her 2017 record deal
entertainment.body:
Summer Walker filed a $20 million cross-complaint against Interscope Records on Wednesday night, escalating a legal battle that began last month when the label first sued the R&B singer , claiming she would owe $50 million if she followed through on a plan to abandon her 2017 recording contract, which industry experts previously described as “brutal.”

The new 10-page cross-complaint, obtained and first reported by Rolling Stone , alleges that Interscope received only limited rights to use Walker’s name, image, and likeness for promotional purposes under a recording agreement she first signed on Nov. 1, 2017. Walker argues that the contract did not grant the label unrestricted rights to profit from her identity or independently created content. She claims Interscope breached the agreement by collecting revenue from her independently created audiovisual recordings, digital content, and personal YouTube channel assets.

Walker, who recently invoked a California labor law known as the “seven-year rule” to terminate her recording contract, is seeking a court declaration that the agreement became unenforceable over the summer, when she notified Interscope of her decision. She also wants the court to affirm her ownership of the disputed assets.

The cross-complaint seeks at least $20 million in damages for the alleged breach of contract alone. It also demands that Interscope’s parent company, Universal Music Group, surrender any profits it improperly earned from the disputed digital assets. The amount of those profits “is unknown and cannot be ascertained without an accounting,” the lawsuit says.

“Summer has always approached her relationship with Interscope in good faith, and she remains appreciative of the role the label has played in her career. However, that relationship does not give Interscope unlimited rights over her creative work or the revenues generated from it,” Walker’s lawyer, Keith Moten, tells Rolling Stone . “Interscope has asserted its interpretation of the parties’ agreement, and Summer is equally entitled to challenge conduct that we believe exceeds the rights granted under that agreement. Tim McGraw was happy to just see his daughters smile at the 2026 CMA Awards .

The “I Like It, I Love It” singer was joined by his and wife Faith Hill ’s daughters Maggie , 28, and Audrey , 24, for the Nov. 18 ceremony as the trio walked the red carpet together before being joined by Faith inside the Bridgestone Arena in Nashville.

The McGraws cut a matching figure for the evening, with Tim, 59, opting for a double-breasted black tuxedo paired with a white dress shirt and his signature black cowboy hat. Audrey looked smashing in a silky black gown, featuring cutout design patterns along the bodice, while sister Maggie donned a sleek black dress with a square neckline and thick black straps.

You’ll like it, you’ll love it that Faith—who also shares daughter Gracie , 29, with Tim—coordinated with the family as well, wearing a low-cut black ensemble for country music’s biggest night.

And coming from a musical family, it only stands to reason that at least one of the McGraw girls—who were all featured on their dad’s 2007 hit “Last Dollar (Fly Away)”—would follow in their parents' footsteps.

And that one is Audrey, who is currently giving her own musical career a go.

In fact, the “I Am…I Said” singer made a surprise appearance at her dad’s concert at the Jones Beach Theater in Wantagh, New York, in July where she performed her mom’s 2002 track “Stronger.”

“I don’t have words to express the honor I feel to sing my mama’s song last night, and for it to be at dad’s show,” Audrey captioned an Instagram post of her performance. “To be your daughter is an infinite gift. Halestorm didn’t go it alone: The Grammy-winning band, with both Hale and Joe Hottinger on guitar, Josh Smith on bass, and Tommy Clufetos on drums (Arejay Hale, the group’s regular drummer had a scheduling conflict), backed up the rest of the guests. entertainment.summary: The CMAs knew Taylor Swift, they knew her. And now, they have gotten to know her again as the singer took the stage to perform at the Country Music Association Awards Nov. 18 in her first CMAs...
entertainment.body:
And now, they have gotten to know her again as the singer took the stage to perform at the Country Music Association Awards Nov. 18 in her first CMAs performance since 2013.

Trading in the yellow Oscar de la Renta gown she wore on the red carpet for a short, white-and-orange frock and cowgirl boots, Swift channeled Toy Story ’s cowgirl character Jessie while singing her Toy Story 5 song "I Knew It, I Knew You."

And she went full yee-haw for her country music return, even turning the performance into a mash-up with her 2007 track “Our Song” from her debut album.

Plus, Swift brought a surprise guest, as she was joined on the banjo by Keith Urban , who she previously collaborated on for her 2021 song "That's When (Taylor's Version) (From The Vault)."

Swift first revealed she’d be stepping back into her cowboy boots in September, when the Toy Story single received its nomination.

“Looks like I haven’t yee’d my last haw,” she joked in an Instagram Story at the time. “Thank you CMA. See you there.”

Meanwhile, Swift—who last attended the ceremony to bestow Garth Brooks with the Entertainer of the Year honor in 2016—has been living by the message sent in her latest country single, admitting she’s found herself returning to her original genre.

“I love my country roots more and more,” Swift said during a conversation at the Grammy Museum in August . “The further along this path I get and I want to honor them more and more, and I feel more tied and more loyal to them. The people that shaped who I am as an artist and as a writer, that all happened in Nashville.”

sports.title: Joe Burrow can become the first QB ever with 4+ touchdowns in 6 consecutive games
sports.summary: Burrow and Peyton Manning are the only QBs ever with 4 TDs in 5 straight games. If Burrow does it again on Monday night, he'll be the first in NFL history to do it in 6 straight games.
sports.body:
Burrow has at least four touchdowns (combined running and passing) in each of the last five games. A four-touchdown game against the Commanders on Monday night would give Burrow an all-time NFL record six straight four-touchdown games.

Currently, Burrow and Peyton Manning are tied for the record, with five consecutive four-touchdown games. Manning did it in 2004 with the Colts. Burrow’s last five games have featured:

Three touchdown passes and one touchdown run in a 34-17 win over the Falcons.

Five touchdown passes and one touchdown run in a 43-36 win over the Titans.

Burrow is the MVP favorite , and with 2,795 yards and 27 touchdown passes through nine games this season, he’s closing in on 3,000 yards and 30 touchdowns, which only four quarterbacks have done within their first 10 games of a season: Tom Brady in 2007, Aaron Rodgers in 2011, Manning in 2013 and 2014, and Patrick Mahomes in 2018. That’s good company for a quarterback to be in, and Burrow is playing right now at a level few quarterbacks have ever reached.

sports.title: Sean Payton won't use Aidan Hutchinson injury as a teaching moment
sports.summary: Lions coach Dan Campbell has made his position clear regarding player celebrations, in the aftermath of defensive end Aidan Hutchinson's season-ending knee injury.
sports.body:
“I’m kind of with Dan,” Payton told reporters. “I saw the final comments. We’re teachers and we’re constantly… But we’re going to walk out of the doors, and there’ve been a lot of celebrations. I’m kind of with Dan there where it’s unfortunate. Two good players got hurt on the same play, and I think that there are a lot of other things that I would put on tape on a Friday, Saturday that are [teaching moments]. That I wouldn’t put that on.”

For starters, any non-contact ACL tear quite possibly is the result of a partially torn knee ligament that was on the brink of fully tearing. If Hutchinson’s ACL tear hadn’t happened when he landed after jumping to celebrate a sack of quarterback Drake Maye, it could have happened on the next play. Or the next.

And it’s impossible to expect players to not celebrate. A great play is the product of hours of work and effort and discipline, most of which happens away from the public eye. In the arena, with thousands cheering and millions watching on TV, how can the human beings inside the uniforms be expected not to display human emotion?

Injuries happen in football. The vast majority happen during a play. Some happen after a play. It’s unreasonable to reduce it to none; the players shouldn’t be expected to minimize or eliminate the happiness they experience when everything they’ve done privately culminates in a public moment of achievement.

sports.title: Kyle Shanahan on the Brian Flores defense: "It's not just a fad"
sports.summary: 49ers coach says the Minnesota defense puts pressure on everyone involved.
sports.body:
They meet again on Sunday night in Mexico City, when Shanahan’s 49ers play the Vikings, whose defense is coordinated by Flores.

“He’s more unique than all the other 31 guys,” Shanahan told reporters on Wednesday regarding Flores. “He’s the one guy who commits to this and it’s not just a fad for these nine games or whatever. He’s been doing it his whole time in Minnesota. He did the same thing in Miami. He’s as good as it gets at that stuff.

“Anybody who lives in that world as much as he does, it’s usually a matter of time. I think offensive coaches used to like to say that early on, but it’s too many years of it and it’s too many games in this year that they’re sound. They put so much pressure on the quarterback, the play-caller, the O-Line, the receivers, on everybody. A lot of times when you go into an NFL game, the pressure’s really on people on third down and stuff like that because those are things where everything can come and when you play against Brian it’s 70-straight plays of that.”

It’s not easy to beat in part because it’s almost impossible to simulate in practice. As Devin McCourty has said, you think you have a plan and then the game starts and everything changes.

It changes in part because Flores seems to be constantly self-scouting and adjusting, defying the films to create pressure in new ways.

The goal is to eliminate the offense’s built-in advantage that comes from knowing what the play will be by creating confusion for the entire offense. Who’s rushing? Who’s dropping into coverage? Who do I block? If that guy doesn’t rush, what do I do?

It makes for a compelling chess match, with the 49ers needing to find a way to get the Minnesota defense on its heels.

A strong running game is a must. Wearing down the defense physically is required. When inevitable passing situations arise, the quarterback needs to quickly find the open man (if there is one) and get the ball out before the walls close in.

sports.title: Nick Bosa: I don't think I've played my best football
sports.summary: 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa's only stats in Sunday's 46-40 win over the Cowboys were one quarterback hit, four pressures and three penalties in 34 snaps.
sports.body:
“I think in the past when I was younger, it would eat at me a lot more , just strictly the stat aspects,” Bosa said Wednesday, via Nick Wagoner of ESPN. “But now I’m really just focused on the people around me, and if I feel like I’m playing good football, then I really don’t care much about the stats. But I don’t think I’m playing my best football right now, so that’s what gets to me more so than the actual stats.”

Bosa exited the injury report in Week 10. But he has worked his way back from the torn ACL in his right knee in Week 3 of the 2025 season and a calf injury in Week 3.

He has played catch up with new coordinator Raheem Morris’ scheme.

“I think there’s a learning curve and . . . a lot of guys haven’t had many reps in the scheme so far,” Bosa said. “I’m trying to break it down to the basics and just kind of get back. I missed a year and then missed camp. I kind of took for granted some of the things that I did automatically, and I thought I could just kind of coast and continue to do those things automatically and focus on other things. But I need to, especially with a newer defense, really hone in on the things that made me the player that I am.”

Bosa’s last double-digit sack season was 2023 when he had 10.5. He totaled nine sacks in 14 games in 2024 and two in three games in 2025, with none this season.

“I’m not going to make excuses because nobody really cares,” Bosa said. “But I’m going to get better and I’m pretty confident in that physically and how I’m playing.”

“As you guys know, I’ve been here my whole career ,” Humphrey said, via Jeff Zrebiec of TheAthletic.com. “Spent lots of offseasons here, welcomed a son here. I’m an investor in the city, an investor in different areas (and) parts of the state. Obviously, I do know the effect that words have, and just would like to apologize for those comments.”

Humphrey’s apology was noted by Baltimore Mayor Brandon M. Scott, who wondered in a social media post how Humphrey would respond “if prominent Baltimoreans used their platform to imply that Baltimore once produced great defensive backs but we have recently lost our way.” Scott added that “a verbal apology is not enough” for those who look up to Ravens players and invited Humphrey to meet with people in the city working on “preventing others from making the mistakes they made.”

sports.body: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bills fans and fans across the country. The 8-1 Buffalo Bills remain one of the most talk-about teams in the NFL this season. They have an all-world quarterback in Josh Allen, and feature a run-first offensive approach led by running back James Cook III and a very talented offensive line that celebrates road grading the rest of the league. Offensively, there’s currently room only to critique things on a microscopic level. It might not always look “conventional,” but it’s impossible to ignore Buffalo’s scoring proficiency. Now, a reformulated defense has settled in a bit, rising to become a middle-of-the-pack group after beginning the season as one of the NFL’s worst stop units. That 8-1 record has the Bills in first place in the AFC, which would grant Buffalo the one seed in the conference and hand them a bye week to begin their playoff run. There’s a ton of football left to play, and that means plenty of scenarios can still play out over the course of the last eight weeks. Which team is the Bills’ biggest threat to their hopes of finally claiming the one seed? There are four very strong candidates, which may or may not set off alarms in your brain. Tight end Dalton Kincaid (thumb, ankle) was one of them. Kincaid was on the injury report because of the ankle last week, but picked up the thumb injury while catching two passes for 58 yards last Sunday.

sports.title: Wilson girls soccer takes home first state championship in program history
sports.summary: The Wilson varsity girls soccer team took home the program's first state championship Sunday night, beating Stillwater 3-0.

sports.title: Eagles claim OL Ajani Cornelius off waivers
sports.summary: The Eagles have added an offensive lineman.
sports.body:
Per the league’s daily transaction wire, Philadelphia has added offensive tackle Ajani Cornelius off of waivers.

A sixth-round pick in 2025, Cornelius has appeared in four games over the last two seasons. He played in three this season, recording 14 special teams snaps.

Coming off a Week 10 bye, the 2-7 Eagles will face the Steelers on Sunday.

sports.title: Cam Skattebo says he's done doing backflips after Aidan Hutchinson injury
sports.summary: Giants running back Cam Skattebo's penchant for backflips became a talking point during his recovery from last season's ankle injury, but he resumed doing them after touchdowns upon his return to action this fall.
sports.body:
Skattebo said that those days are now done, however. Skattebo said on Wednesday that he’s retiring the celebration in the wake of seeing Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson tear his ACL after a post-sack celebratory leap last Sunday.

“It’s hard to see ,” Skattebo said, via Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post . “I’m saying yeah [no more]. Mentally, I’m like, ‘I’m not doing that.’ That ain’t going to happen to me.”

Skattebo did reserve the right to bring the celebration out of retirement “if we go to the playoffs or something,” but it seems any touchdowns in the immediate future will be marked with a more reserved reaction.

He watched practice Wednesday, while rookie Jalon Daniels ran the first team.

Cornerback Josh Hayes (knee), tight end Cade Otton (thumb) and offensive tackle Tristan Wirfs (toe) were full participants.

sports.title: Titans get Carnell Tate back at practice
sports.summary: The Titans won't be getting wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson back on the field this season, but they could be getting first-round pick Carnell Tate back in the lineup against the Cowboys this week.
sports.body:
Tate was able to practice on a limited basis on Wednesday. He missed the last two games with a shoulder injury and had 34 catches for 413 yards and a touchdown in the first seven games of the season.

sports.title: Lions place Aidan Hutchinson on IR, activate Kerby Joseph
sports.summary: While one Lions player is out, another is on his way back in.
sports.body:
Detroit announced on Wednesday afternoon that the club has placed defensive end Aidan Hutchinson on injured reserve and activated safety Kerby Joseph off of the reserve/physically unable to perform list.

Hutchinson suffered a torn ACL during the Lions’ victory over the Patriots in Munich on Sunday. It’s the second season-ending injury in the last three years for Hutchinson, who missed most of 2024 with a fractured tibia and fibula.

Joseph has been sidelined by knee issues that limited him to six games last season. He was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice. Head coach Dan Campbell has said that Joseph is expected to play against Tampa Bay on Sunday.

Additionally, the Lions have re-signed defensive back Nick Whiteside to the club’s practice squad.

“I did want to give you guys some encouraging news on Jordan Addison,” O’Connell said, via the team’s website. “The updates following the surgery, he will not, as of right now, go on short-term IR. Just looking at the potential timeline for that, so that was really encouraging . Obviously subject to change as he gets into his rehab. He joined us back here today, and we’re excited to get him going.”

sports.title: Brian Schottenheimer: Christian Parker still has a bright future with the Cowboys
sports.summary: Brian Schottenheimer confirmed Mike Pettine will take over as the Cowboys' defensive play-caller on Sunday.
sports.body:
“Christian Parker is a huge part of what we’re trying to build here and that he is our defensive coordinator,” Schottenheimer said Wednesday, via Todd Archer of ESPN. “He is our leader. He is not changing any of those things, but I do feel that in the best interest of winning that Pet’s calling the game is going to help us get to where we want to get to.”

Schottenheimer said Parker would continue running meetings and leading walkthroughs, but the Cowboys needed “a different perspective” on game day.

Parker, 34, arrived in January as a first-time play caller, leaving Philadelphia after two seasons as the Eagles’ defensive passing game coordinator. The Cowboys, though, rank last in yards (393.8), last in run defense (154.1) and last in third-down defense (48.8 percent). They are 30th in scoring (28.2).

Pettine arrived before Week 5 as a senior defensive assistant to help Parker, whom he brought into the NFL with the Packers in 2019. He was defensive coordinator with the Jets, when Schottenheimer was on staff, and also served in that role with the Bills and Packers.

“When I look at this situation, we’re all committed to trying to get it right,” Schottenheimer said, “and so we’re making adjustments like we’ve made. We’ve made adjustments. We’ve adjusted some scheme. We’ve adjusted some personnel. We’ve adjusted some play time. This is just another adjustment where we’re trying to get right.”

Schottenheimer made clear several times that he still believes in Parker and still believes Parker has a future with the Cowboys.

“CP has a very, very bright future as a coach, but more specifically, a very bright future here as our defense coordinator,” Schottenheimer said.

sports.title: Kenneth Walker won't practice Wednesday with groin injury
sports.summary: Kenneth Walker's groin injury will keep him out for at least another day.
sports.body:
Head coach Andy Reid told reporters in his press conference that the running back is one of a few players who won’t practice on Wednesday.

“He’s got a sore groin, so it’s getting better. But with those … you don’t want to do something stupid, going out there,” Reid said. “It’s still bugging him a little bit. But he’s feeling a lot better than he was.

“We’ll just see. It’s a day-to-day thing, so we’ll see how it goes.”

Walker did not practice last Friday before missing Sunday’s victory over the Falcons. Rookie Emmett Johnson rushed for 101 yards and had six catches for 70 yards with two touchdowns in Walker’s stead.

Additionally, Reid said right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) and right guard Trey Smith (concussion protocol) will not practice on Wednesday.

The full first injury report of the week for Kansas City will be released later in the day.

sports.title: After earning their first win, Chargers are favored to win their second vs. Jets
sports.summary: The Chargers finally won a game on Monday.
sports.body:
It’s not often that a 1-8 team is favored, but the Chargers are 3.5-point favorites on Sunday against the Jets.

That’s not an indication that anyone is buying into the Chargers after they beat the Ravens on Monday night, as the Chargers opened as favorites even before they won a game. It’s more a reflection of how bad the 2-8 Jets are, that they’re not a safe bet to beat anyone.

The Chargers were favored in the first two weeks of the season, by 9.5 against the Cardinals in Week 1 and by 6.5 against the Chargers in Week 2. They lost both games by 12, and since then they’ve been underdogs every week.

This is the ninth time this season the Jets have been underdogs. They were last favored in Week 7, when they were favored by four points over the Dolphins but lost 28-25.

In a game between two of the worst teams in the league, someone has to win, and the betting odds say that someone will be the Chargers.

sports.title: Sean Mannion to continue calling offensive plays for Eagles, Joe Milton to remain at QB
sports.summary: Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said that the team would talk about changes to roles and responsibilities on the coaching staff during their bye week, but he said on Wednesday that they decided against any major ones.
sports.body:
That means offensive coordinator Sean Mannion will continue calling the team’s offensive plays when they face the Steelers this week. Sirianni explained why he’s staying the course at a Wednesday press conference.

“I think he’s really smart. I think he has a great football mind,” Sirianni said, via a transcript from the team. “He thinks through everything. I think one thing I always value about him is [that] anybody can come and give a play and say, ‘Hey, I want to do this, or I want to do that.’ I think he just has a really good monotonous approach to figuring out everything that could potentially happen in that situation, what the downfalls are, what the upside is and whether we move forward with some of those things. I think that just speaks to the detail that he has. It hasn’t gone well enough for any of us this year offensively. That’s coaches, that’s players. We all have things that we need to do better, but I do love that approach that he has with that. As we looked at some of our schemes that he’s brought in, some of those have been really, really good. It has to be better as a whole without getting too much into the specifics of what those are. We just need to build on that.”

Mannion will be sending the play calls in to quarterback Joe Milton for the second straight game. He was 18-of-34 for 169 yards while running nine times for 64 yards and losing a fumble in a Week 9 loss to the Giants.

“He works extremely hard with everything,” Sirianni said. “Really love his approach, like his personality, but I really appreciate his approach to how he goes through everything.”

The loss to the Giants was the seventh in a row for the Eagles. They’ll try to avoid their first eight-game slide since 2012 this week.

sports.title: Todd Bowles: Baker Mayfield's made progress, decision on playing to come on Friday
sports.summary: Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield missed practice on Wednesday with a foot injury, but the team hasn't made a decision on his availability for Sunday's game against the Lions.

But he’s a lot better than he was a week ago. I don’t know if that’s ready or not. I want to see it for myself and we’ll see what he can do tomorrow.”

sports.title: Buffalo Bills Week 10 snap counts: Defensive rotation and injuries stand out in win over Jets
sports.summary: The Buffalo Bills improved their position in the AFC East with a 31-12 victory over the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on Sunday Buffalo’s offense played just 57 snaps compared to 71 for the defense. The Jets held a 32:01 to 27:59 advantage in time of possession, but Buffalo made its opportunities
sports.body: The Buffalo Bills improved their position in the AFC East with a 31-12 victory over the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on Sunday Buffalo’s offense played just 57 snaps compared to 71 for the defense. The Jets held a 32:01 to 27:59 advantage in time of possession, but Buffalo made its opportunities count, producing 389 total yards and four touchdowns. While the Jets finished with a 32:01 to 27:59 advantage in time of possession, that statistic doesn’t tell the entire story. Buffalo actually controlled the clock in the first half, holding the ball for 18:36 compared to New York’s 11:24. The second half was a different story, largely because the Bills’ offense simply didn’t need much time to score. Buffalo produced three touchdown drives totaling just seven offensive plays and 2:49 of possession. Josh Allen capped a four-play drive with a rushing touchdown, connected with DJ Moore on a 45-yard score during a two-play possession, and James Cook put the game away with a 74-yard touchdown run on the first play of another drive. Those three possessions accounted for 21 points in less than three minutes. The defense certainly had its share of extended drives to contend with, but Buffalo’s explosive offensive production played a significant role in the disparity between offensive and defensive snap counts. Offensive snap counts The Bills’ offensive line remained relatively consistent throughout the afternoon. Left tackle Dion Dawkins and right guard O’Cyrus Torrence played all 57 snaps, while Connor McGovern, Alec Anderson, and Spencer Brown each played 54 (95%). Josh Allen also played 54 snaps before Kyle Allen entered for the final three plays. At running back, James Cook led the group with 35 snaps (61%), followed by Ray Davis with 12 (21%) and Ty Johnson with 10 (18%). Cook made the most of his opportunities, rushing for 157 yards and a touchdown on 18 carries, including a 74-yard scoring run in the fourth quarter. The wide receiver rotation was more evenly distributed. Khalil Shakir led the group with 36 snaps (63%), followed by DJ Moore with 33 (58%), Keon Coleman with 30 (53%), and Skyler Bell with 20 (35%). The tight end usage was particularly interesting. Dawson Knox led the position with 41 snaps (72%), while Jackson Hawes and Dalton Kincaid each played 26 (46%). sports.body: The Buffalo Bills have loved running the football thus far in the 2026 season. James Cook has the second-most carries in the NFL right now at 187. As a team, the Bills are the current owners of the second-highest first-down designed run rate in the NFL at 61.3%. Now, sure, the Bills have recently played in a collection of games that featured plenty of garbage time, when Buffalo has attempted to burn clock by tapping into the run game. Even when garbage-time is considered, the Bills have the NFL’s second-highest run rate on all downs at 45.7%. The rest of the league averages a designed run play on 39.3%. Quarterback scrambles — that occur on dropbacks — and spikes and kneels are excluded in that calculation. Analytics have proven that passing the football is more efficient than running the football. sports.body: Sometimes, important additions to an NFL team don’t occur until close to September… or even in-season. On August 18, after their first preseason game, the Bills signed veteran defensive lineman Greg Gaines — potentially as a response to rookie defensive tackle Zane Durant being injured late in the opening exhibition game against the Panthers. Almost exactly two weeks later, on the last day of August, as the team seemingly had no clear-cut candidate to return punts, Buffalo scooped up Greg Dortch after he was surprisingly cut by the Lions. Through the first nine games of the season, both have provided valuable, low-key contributions to this Bills team. On the surface, Gaines’ presence has been irrelevant. He has 11 tackles and one tackles for loss along with two pressures on 77 pass-rush snaps on 22.5% of Buffalo’s defensive snaps. But when Gaines is on the field, he’s a magnet for blockers, which has a massive ripple effect on his teammates. More blockers on him, fewer on other Bills defenders. Gaines is currently 10th in the NFL among qualifying defensive linemen in double-team rate (67.5%) on pass-rush snaps. It’s the highest rate on Buffalo’s roster right now (among qualifiers). As for Dortch, the value he’s added has been easier to discern. Among punt returners with at least 15 returns to date, his 9.2 yards-per-return average is seventh-best in the NFL. He’s been darn good as a kicker returner too, so teams aren’t able to simply directionally kick it away from reigning All-Pro kicker returner Ray Davis. While Davis is second in the NFL in average kick-return yardage at 29.6 entering Week 11, Dortch is tied for 12th with an average of 27.2 yards per kick return. And he’s actually returned nearly double the amount of kickoffs (23) as Davis (12). And then there’s Amani Hooker. Of course, the jury is still out on how much the trade-deadline acquisition will impact Buffalo’s defense. But in his first game, after a week of practice in a new scheme on a new team, he played the most defensive snaps of any Bills defender (70), made seven tackles, and had a pass breakup that was nearly an interception. sports.body: The New York Jets have solicited advice from nearly everyone on planet Earth when hiring head coaches this century. That has included The 33rd Team, Charley Casserly, and do you remember that one time when Pro Football Hall of Famer Peyton Manning made a phone call to seal the deal for Adam Gase? Great times. That can’t happen in 2027. Make no mistake about it: the Jets will be looking for a new head coach in a matter of months, but in all of those other situations, they lost the battle before it ever began. Stop relying on people outside of the building. Put your big boy pants on and make a decision for yourself. Who is the right man for that job? Darren Mougey. Woody Johnson has called Mougey “The General” this offseason when referencing him to fans. He has spoken highly of him and believes the team is going in the right direction because of Mougey. Put him in the driver’s seat for this search and allow him to vet the candidates. ESPN New York’s Jake Asman called the latest Jets HC search a “sham” on the “Jets Collective” podcast. “Woody Johnson put Mike Tannenbaum, Rick Spielman, and The 33rd Team in charge of vetting candidates. Liam Coen is a UMass alum, Mike Tannenbaum went to UMass, and again, I work with Mike, so I’m comfortable saying this to his face. We’ve had many battles on the air and off the air, but if [the] Coz reporting is right that they got the intel wrong on Liam Coen, it’s another indictment of just this sham of a search process that led to Aaron Glenn.” --- J-E-T-S! sports.body: The Buffalo Bills announced a series of roster moves as they begin preparations to host the Miami Dolphins at Highmark Stadium for Week 11. Buffalo has signed defensive back Te’Cory Couch to the practice squad, bringing him back to One Bills Drive after being released ahead of last weekend’s game and once he cleared waivers Monday afternoon. The 27-year-old defender out of the University of Miami has played in four games for Buffalo this season. In those games, Couch has made eight tackles (6 solo), showcasing a knack for limiting big plays after the catch with solid tackling. Couch joined the Bills in 2024, entering the NFL as an undrafted rookie free agent. To make room for Couch, Buffalo once again parted ways with veteran offensive guard Nick Broeker, who has been re-added to the team’s practice squad several times already this season. Broeker has yet to appear in a regular-season game for the Bills, though he has previously played in 12 games (2023 and 2024 seasons) for the Denver Broncos. Broeker was originally drafted by Buffalo in Round 7 (230th overall) of the 2023 NFL Draft. The Bills also announced that rookie offensive guard Ar’maj Reed-Adams has been placed on Injured Reserve, which will sideline him for at least the next four games. With Reed-Adams heading to IR, that opens up a spot on Buffalo’s 53-man roster. A potential candidate to take over that roster opening is veteran wide receiver Tyrell Shavers, whose return-to-practice window was recently opened as the next step toward a return to the field following a devastating knee injury against the Jacksonville Jaguars during the Bills’ 2025 NFL playoff run.

In the first six games of the 2026 season, wh
sports.body: Yes, the Buffalo Bills have gone from a gauntlet of high-level quarterbacks to start to the season to a consecutive collection of backups, and that drastic shift in competition has coincided with a drastic shift in defensive philosophy from Jim Leonhard. In the first six games of the 2026 season, when Buffalo’s defense was a liability, the Bills played man coverage 16.4% of the time, per Fantasy Points Data. That was the 24th-highest man-coverage rate in the NFL. Also in those first six outings, Buffalo’s blitz rate was 27.9%, the 20th-highest blitz rate in football. Then the bye week happened. Since then, the Bills’ man-coverage rate jumped to 25.7%. In that three-game sample, that’s the 13th-highest in the league. Buffalo’s blitz rate has been 33.6% combined in Weeks 8, 9, and 10, the 13th-highest blitz rate in the NFL. (Can’t forget too — there was plenty of garbage time in all three contests, where the Bills, like any team, were prompted to sit back in soft zone to keep everything in front of them.) The new man-coverage and blitz rates don’t represent massive, 180-degree changes in philosophy. And we likely won’t be able to fully discern how much Leonhard’s man-coverage and blitzing movement post-bye has actually made the Bills defense better until Thanksgiving night against Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. But one thing is for sure — Leonhard’s defense has recently started to look like what we expected Leonhard’s defense to look like all along.

sports.body: We have seven more games left in the Aaron Glenn era for the New York Jets. I will not remember this time period fondly whatsoever, but don’t worry, because there is a light at the end of the tunnel. ESPN’s Rich Cimini said on the “Jets Collective” podcast that he could potentially see the team making an aggressive move to trade for their next head coach. Cimini said, “The name I would watch for is KOC, Kevin O’Connell. I was just talking to a couple of people in the league today, and they said they could see [Darren] Mougey giving up a high draft pick for Kevin O’Connell. They went to college together; they have maintained a relationship. If something falls apart there in Minnesota, if they collapse down the stretch, or if they decide that they want to elevate [Brian] Flores instead of losing him to another team, maybe they make that move.” Cimini revealed that, “I was told Mougey even in meetings like offseason and preseason has spoken, internal meetings with the Jets has spoken highly of O’Connell has mentioned him in meetings and so I wouldn’t totally dismiss that. I mean, he would come in, they would get along great, they have a history, he is an offensive-minded coach with coaching experience. Now, he has made a couple of questionable quarterback decisions in Minnesota. I don’t know how much of that is him or the GM or the previous GM, but I think it’s a name to watch for; let me put that out there.” Oh baby! Spicy! Sexy! Interesting! Now I’m sure there will be a huge debate in the comment section about whether this is too crazy or even worth it. Before you run to the comments, I would just like to provide some statistical data about KOC. The Jets, in their team history, have only ever won 12 games in a regular season once (1998). O’Connell is in his fifth season as a head coach in the NFL. He has already surpassed that number twice with a 14-win season (2024) and a 13-win season (2022). Who knows if he will add a third such year to his resume; the Vikings are currently 7-2. KOC is awesome, and if the Jets can find a way, they should absolutely explore it. --- J-E-T-S!
